headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while BTC quietly leaves exchange wallets
paragraphs: Start with structure, because it's unanimous today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day averages, none showing a golden cross. Distance from twelve-month highs ranges from BTC's relatively modest -49.2% to ADA's -79.9%, with ETH at -61.5%, SOL at -70.3%, XRP at -67.6%, BNB at -55.0% and DOGE at -75.8%. Seven-for-seven below trend is a single, consistent regime, not a mixed picture.

Momentum tells a more interesting story than trend alone. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 47 with MACD below signal, and price is essentially idle: -0.13% on the day, -1.45% over seven days, -0.87% over thirty. That's a market resting, not breaking down further. ADA is the outlier worth naming: RSI 67.8, MACD above signal, up 17.38% over seven days and 22.16% over thirty, yet still 79.9% off its high and under its 200-day line. That's momentum sharply diverging from structure. BNB and DOGE also show MACD crossed above signal despite sitting below trend, a quiet thaw in momentum that hasn't yet dragged the longer-term picture with it.

Positioning leans long almost everywhere. Long/short account ratios run from BTC's 1.64 up to DOGE's 4.84, with XRP at 3.09 and SOL at 2.67. Funding is mildly positive across the board (BTC 3.1% annualized, SOL 7.2%, XRP 6.3%, DOGE 5.0%) except ETH, which sits at -0.3% annualized, longs paying nothing and shorts actually collecting a sliver. That negative ETH funding lines up with its liquidation tape: $10.1M in longs wiped out over 24 hours versus $3.5M in shorts. Open interest in BTC ($1.97B) and ETH ($1.33B) is substantial, but funding levels this modest mean the long tilt isn't expensive yet, crowded in direction, not in cost.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs posted +$18.6M on 03 Aug, but that sits inside a five-session net of -$31.3M with same_direction_days at just 1, one green print inside a red stretch. ETH ETFs were negative both ways: -$7.8M on the day, -$9.5M over five sessions. Stablecoin float slipped -1.02% over thirty days, a small thinning of dry powder. Meanwhile the whale ledger shows $103.1M net moving off exchanges in 24 hours, entirely in BTC, anchored by a $51.55M move off Coinbase Institutional. The four-period weekly trend accelerates this: -$21.9M, then $83.5M, then $816.99M, then $911.9M net leaving exchanges, a genuine multi-session drift toward cold storage. Yet the stablecoin side of the ledger reads -$133.3M in "buying power," meaning the cash sitting ready to deploy on exchanges thinned too, not just the coins.

Sentiment is Extreme Fear at 25, near the bottom of its own 30-day band of 20 to 33. That reading sits awkwardly next to a tape showing BTC quietly leaving exchange wallets in growing weekly size and one positive ETF print breaking a losing streak. Fear and flow aren't agreeing, and that gap is the day's real story more than any single number.

What would change the picture: any major reclaiming its 200-day line, the BTC or ETH ETF five-session net flipping positive with same_direction_days climbing past one, funding turning meaningfully negative across the board rather than just in ETH, or the stablecoin float resuming growth instead of its current -1.02% drift. On the network side, fees remain parked at 1 sat/vB with difficulty up 1.6% over the last 691-block retarget, so miners are pressing on regardless of what price is doing.
